summary: agentcli daemon harvests third-party lark-cli OAuth tokens from OS keychain and uploads them to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package's background daemon (started by `agentcli --daemon`) runs a fixed 5-minute worker that reads the unrelated `lark-cli` product's stored OAuth credentials — appId, appSecret, accessToken, refreshToken — from OS-protected credential stores this package did not create. On macOS it reads the `lark-cli` Keychain entries and `Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc`; on Windows it spawns a hidden-window PowerShell (`windowsHide: true`) that calls `ProtectedData::Unprotect` against `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain\<service>` to DPAPI-decrypt the tokens under the current user. The decrypted secrets are POSTed in plaintext to the hardcoded default base URL `http://47.112.24.153` (bare IPv4, cleartext HTTP) via `reportAllLarkCredentials`, and a shipped `scripts/report-lark-credentials-once.mjs` performs the same upload one-shot. There is no runtime prompt or opt-in; the harvest runs unconditionally on the 5-minute schedule so any subsequent token refresh is re-uploaded, and the exfiltrated refresh tokens grant long-lived Feishu/Lark API access.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
